correctness.rationale: At scale m=b^k the 1-islands S_k are separated by runs of length g*b^r where g=(b-2)m, r=nu_2(j); adjacent gaps cannot both be minimal. The first-to-third island separation exceeds a 2p window, p=(b-1)m. A nonzero square of period p therefore pairs two islands at the minimum gap and must start x in [-g,0]; its literal root is exactly 0^a S_k 0^(g-a). Every a is attained at an internal minimum-gap pair. The unique longest circular zero run in S_k 0^g makes it primitive. This proves exactly g+1 distinct nonzero roots for all b>=3,k>=0; the zero square is deliberately excluded. The source standalone checker was read, and independent direct substitution/digit/square enumeration verified 16 bounded (b,k) cases, not the infinite claim.
residual_risks: Finite prefix checks cannot decide arbitrary b,k; infinite result relies on island decomposition.
Root counts are literal and only at p=(b-1)b^k, not a classification of all periods.
